hypotheses.justification: The proof uses `ha` only through `chart_contDiff ha` (smoothness of `chart a j`); after that it needs only continuity of the iterated derivatives on the compact ball. `chart a j` is smooth for every real `a`. It is `extendedBase a ∘ rotate j` plus a constant offset, where `extendedBase a p = (√(positiveRadius (a²/32) (p.1²+p.2²)), arctan (p.2 / positiveRadius (a/8) p.1))` and `positiveRadius ℓ x = ℓ + (x-ℓ)·smoothTransition((x-ℓ)/ℓ)`, which is smooth for every ℓ (`positiveRadius_contDiff`). Case a = 0: `positiveRadius 0 x = x·smoothTransition (x/0) = x·smoothTransition 0 = 0`, so `extendedBase 0 p = (√0, arctan (p.2/0)) = (0,0)` and the chart is the constant `(0, offset j)`, smooth by `contDiff_const`. Case a < 0: the radius part has ℓ = a²/32 > 0, so `positiveRadius_pos` gives a positive argument to the square root as before. The angle part has ℓ = a/8 < 0, and `positiveRadius ℓ x` is never zero: if x ≥ ℓ then (x-ℓ)/ℓ ≤ 0, so the value is ℓ < 0; if x ≤ 2ℓ then (x-ℓ)/ℓ ≥ 1, so the value is x < 0; if 2ℓ < x < ℓ then x-ℓ < 0 and smoothTransition is positive, so the value is < ℓ < 0. Hence `ContDiff.div` and `arctan` apply as in `extendedBase_contDiff`. Case a > 0: this is the existing `chart_contDiff`. With `ContDiff ℝ ∞ (chart a j)` for all a, the rest of the proof (`IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn`, summing the bounds over the finite set Index × Fin (m+1)) goes through unchanged, including the degenerate cases b < 0 (empty ball) and m = 0.
